clue.text: Goddam PC! Our service includes protection against leaks

indicators.note: the run of words is said to include the answer, so it sits inside them, spanning the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run from the end of Goddam, through PC and Our, into the start of service

explanation.surface: Someone swears at their computer while noting that their plumbing service covers leaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation makes Goddam PC look like an outburst, but it simply carries the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp course is a waterproof layer built into a wall to stop moisture rising, a barrier against seepage.

clue.text: Handy editor turned up on newspaper

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first
in a down clue, turning something up means reading it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for editor
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A useful editor is promoted at a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy can mean skilful with the hands, which is what being nimble and dexterous amounts to.

clue.text: Certain to support Middle East area bill

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes after the others

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for Middle East
A is the abbreviation for area
sure is a synonym of certain

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to back a bill concerning the Middle East region.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like an invoice, but here it is a piece of proposed legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is a legislative proposal or act, the parliamentary sense of a bill before the house.

clue.text: Homer delivering a message?

parts.note: surface reading: the Greek poet Homer passing on some news, or perhaps Homer Simpson
setter's reading: a homer is a bird trained to fly back home, used to carry notes

explanation.definitionFit: A bird trained to return to its loft was used to carry written notes strapped to its leg, so it is a homing message-bearer.

clue.text: Screen broadcast "Rub me all over!"

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
all over the place suggests disorder, reinforcing that the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A racy line is shouted out on air, perhaps in a suncream advert.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella shields you from rain or sun, and figuratively any protective cover is a shelter or shield.

clue.text: Small friar wedged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's portly companion

explanation.definitionFit: Something wedged tight is jammed in place and cannot be moved, which is the meaning of the past participle here.

clue.text: Unpleasant niff from chamberpot no good

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot, a bedroom toilet bowl
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A nasty smell is coming from a chamber pot that is past it.
explanation.walkthrough: Niff is British slang for a smell; pong is the British word for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A pong is a strong bad smell in British slang, so it matches a nasty niff exactly.

clue.text: Chap spilling seed starts to damage our nasturtiums continually

parts.note: in Genesis Onan spilled his seed on the ground rather than father a child

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters only

parts.note: the initial letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A gardener is spilling seed and damaging the nasturtiums.
explanation.definitionFit: On and on describes something going without stopping, the idiom for endlessly or without pause.

clue.text: Old Barnet fishmonger might have this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Barnet (from Barnet Fair) is cockney rhyming slang for hair, so an old person's hairdo, a mullet gone grey
second meaning: a sea fish sold on a fishmonger's slab

explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is also a London borough, which the surface plays on; a mullet is the short-at-front, long-at-back haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A greying mullet haircut suits an elderly head, and the same name is a common grey-scaled food fish.

clue.text: Douglas is one to embrace US city stylishness

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the Douglas fir is a kind of tree
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A man called Douglas is set to take a stylish American city to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas looks like a person's name but is the Douglas fir.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair means a natural talent for elegance and style, so it matches stylishness as a noun.

clue.text: She's found in the depths, depressed with husband, bitter

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling low
W is the abbreviation for with
H is the abbreviation for husband
bitter is a type of British ale

explanation.surface: A woman sinks into despair, low and resentful about her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The depths suggests depression, but it is the deep ocean; bitter is a hoppy British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest animal ever lives in the open ocean and dives deep, so a female one is found in the depths.

clue.text: Teddy's option, when he and I will get drunk

indicators.note: being drunk means reeling and confused, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: the letters of option, when, he and I; the and only joins them

explanation.surface: Someone named Teddy chooses a moment for a drinking session with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy reads as a man's name, but it is a teddy bear, the bear of very little brain created by A. A. Milne.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh is the most famous stuffed toy bear in children's literature, an example of a teddy.

clue.text: EU not kidding about beginning to manipulate our country

indicators.note: about means moving around, so the letters are shifted into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken letter for letter

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of manipulate

explanation.surface: A seriously meant warning that Europe is trying to steer Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is a British paper, so our country is the setter's own nation.
explanation.definitionFit: For a British newspaper's readers the home nation is Britain, formally the state of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

clue.text: It's packed in the Tube for Hampstead Heath, according to cockney!

definitions.text: It's packed in the Tube for Hampstead Heath, according to cockney!

parts.words: packed in the Tube for Hampstead Heath
parts.note: surface reading: crowds crammed on the London Underground heading for the park at Hampstead Heath
setter's reading: in cockney rhyming slang Hampstead Heath means teeth, so this is something squeezed from a tube for cleaning them

explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground; Hampstead Heath is a large park in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental paste comes squeezed in a soft tube and is used for brushing teeth, the meaning of the slang phrase.

clue.text: Finished game of rugby the French declare invalid

parts.note: over means ended
RU stands for rugby union
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A referee rules a finished French rugby match void.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrule a decision is to reject or set it aside using higher authority, making it void.

clue.text: Remarkable design, all-weather trousers

indicators.note: as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the words pocket the answer inside them

parts.note: the end of design runs into the start of all-weather

explanation.surface: An advert praises the striking design of some waterproof trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Trousers looks like a noun but is the verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, signal means notable or conspicuous, as in a signal achievement or victory.

clue.text: Hero's lover carrying old flowering shrub

indicators.note: carrying means holding something, so one piece is held by the other

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to reach Hero

explanation.surface: A mythical lover brings an ancient shrub in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous Mediterranean evergreen bush with pink or white blossoms.

clue.text: Lunch at home following quarrel

indicators.note: the first-named piece comes after the second, so it is placed later

parts.note: a tiff is a minor squabble
in means at home

explanation.surface: A couple have lunch at home after a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light midday meal, used for a packed lunch.

clue.text: Conifer Starmer regularly carried in sack

indicators.note: carried in means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is used

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Starmer

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer, the British prime minister, is routinely carried off in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The fir is an evergreen cone-bearing tree, so it is a typical example of the kind.

clue.text: Everyone in that place completely sane

parts.note: all means everyone
there means in that place

explanation.surface: Everyone present is of sound mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all there is an idiom for being mentally alert and in full possession of your wits.

clue.text: Having principals, I teach unruly student

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are set in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken letter for letter
L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: A school head admits teaching a disruptive pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: Principals is a deliberate pun on principles, fitting the school setting with its head teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical means having moral standards or principles; the misspelling is the setter's joke about school heads.

clue.text: Quiet new Ritz Hotel accommodating Lincoln City formerly

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for soft

indicators.note: a hotel accommodating a guest houses them, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the letters of Ritz Hotel rearranged
Abe is Abraham Lincoln's short name

explanation.surface: A quiet, newly refurbished Ritz hotel is hosting guests from Lincoln City football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln City looks like the English football club, but City formerly is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Elizabeth is the South African coastal city renamed Gqeberha in 2021, so it is a former name.

clue.text: Help part of the UK, backing the country

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: aid means help
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Supporting one region of Britain while also backing the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation in South Asia, so it is an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: River goes into inlet in village on the Thames

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river flows into an estuary near a Thameside village.
explanation.definitionFit: Bray is a Berkshire village beside the river west of London, known for its famous restaurants.

clue.text: Crooned at Ms Williams, beginning to duet with Mr Sheeran

parts.note: Serena Williams, the tennis champion

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of duet
Ed Sheeran, the singer-songwriter

explanation.surface: Ed Sheeran sings to Serena Williams, starting a duet with her.
explanation.definitionFit: To serenade someone is to sing or play music to them, often romantically, so crooned at fits in the past tense.

clue.text: Prestigious award that comes after November?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Academy Award statuette given in Hollywood
second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for O follows the one for N

explanation.walkthrough: November reads as the month, as if an awards season follows it, but it is the radio code word for N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the film industry's top honour, and the same word is the radio code for the letter O.

clue.text: Study following Eton's first Tory PM

indicators.note: the first-named piece is placed after the next one
the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Eton
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: A Conservative prime minister studied after leaving Eton, the elite school.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was a Conservative prime minister from 1955 to 1957, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Fresh pear with a garnish of cold cheese

indicators.note: a garnish surrounds a dish, so the second piece is placed around the first
fresh means newly made, so the letters are formed anew

parts.note: the letters of pear rearranged
chilly means cold

explanation.surface: A recipe: a fresh pear served with a cold garnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Caerphilly is a crumbly white Welsh cheese, named after the town in south Wales.
